name: bikestores_ambiguity
_notes: Ambiguous cases use neutral phrasing that genuinely maps to two join paths in the BikeStores schema graph. The interpretation the simulated user wants is declared by 'intent' (human-readable) and 'clarification_path_index' (which of the two path-ordered options the user clicks: 0 = shortest/most-direct path, 1 = longer path through an intermediate table). The pair of stocked-vs-ordered cases share identical wording on purpose: the baseline can satisfy at most one with a single blind guess, while the full pipeline asks and reaches whichever the user confirmed.
Each ambiguous gold answer was verified to differ materially from its sibling on the real data (313 vs 226 products; 2 vs 3 staff).
Control cases are unambiguous (a single join path or one table). The full pipeline should match the baseline and should NOT ask a clarifying question; spurious questions are measured.

cases.question: How many different products are associated with the store 'Santa Cruz Bikes'?
cases.intent: Products currently stocked in that store's own inventory (stores -> stocks -> products).
cases.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS product_count FROM stores s JOIN stocks st ON st.store_id = s.store_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = st.product_id WHERE s.store_name = 'Santa Cruz Bikes';

cases.question: How many different products are associated with the store 'Santa Cruz Bikes'?
cases.intent: Products that have actually been ordered through that store (stores -> orders -> order_items -> products).
cases.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS product_count FROM stores s JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE s.store_name = 'Santa Cruz Bikes';

cases.question: How many staff members are associated with customer 1?
cases.intent: Staff who personally processed this customer's orders (customers -> orders -> staffs).
cases.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.staff_id) AS staff_count FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = 1;

cases.question: How many staff members are associated with customer 1?
cases.intent: All staff working at the store(s) this customer ordered from (customers -> orders -> stores -> staffs).
cases.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT st.staff_id) AS staff_count FROM orders o JOIN staffs st ON st.store_id = o.store_id WHERE o.customer_id = 1;

cases.question: How many customers are registered in total?
cases.intent: A single-table count with no join, so no ambiguity is possible.
cases.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers;

cases.question: How many products are in each category? Show the category name.
cases.intent: Products join categories along a single path (products -> categories); unambiguous.
cases.expected_sql: SELECT c.category_name, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products p JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id GROUP BY c.category_name ORDER BY c.category_name;

cases.question: How many products does each brand have? Show the brand name.
cases.intent: Products join brands along a single path (products -> brands); unambiguous.
cases.expected_sql: SELECT b.brand_name, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products p JOIN brands b ON b.brand_id = p.brand_id GROUP BY b.brand_name ORDER BY b.brand_name;
